uncited: This method defines a comprehensive protocol for evaluating the geometric, photometric, and procedural quality of 3D reconstruction systems, particularly those involving Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) and SLAM.
It addresses the need to quantify both static reconstruction fidelity and dynamic tracking performance.

It distinguishes itself from [Mesh Quality Evaluation](8534-mesh-quality-evaluation.md) by focusing on point-cloud-based geometric distances and SLAM-specific trajectory errors, and from [Evaluation Pipeline](9358-evaluation-pipeline.md) by providing the specific mathematical definitions for accuracy, completeness, and photometric metrics.
- **Inputs**: Predicted mesh (or implicit field), ground truth mesh, predicted depth maps, ground truth depth maps, camera poses, and ground truth camera poses.
- **Outputs**: Scalar metrics for Accuracy, Completion, Completion Ratio, ATE RMSE, PSNR, Depth L1, and Normal Consistency.
**Geometric Accuracy (Acc)**: The mean distance from predicted points to the ground truth surface.
**Geometric Completion (Comp)**: The mean distance from ground truth points to the predicted surface.
**Completion Ratio (Comp. [%])**: The proportion of extracted meshes where the Completion value is smaller than 5 cm.
**Precision (Prec)**: The proportion of predicted points within a threshold (0.05) of the ground truth.
**Recall (Recall)**: The proportion of ground truth points within a threshold (0.05) of the predicted surface.
**F-score**: The harmonic mean of Precision and Recall.
**Normal Consistency**: The mean dot product of predicted and ground truth normals at corresponding points.
where $\bar{p}$ is the closest point to $p$ in $\bar{P}$.
**Chamfer-L1 Distance**: The sum of Accuracy and Completion.
**Camera Trajectory Accuracy (ATE RMSE)**: The Root Mean Square Error of the camera trajectory.
**Photometric Precision (PSNR)**: Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio of the estimated depth.
**Depth L1**: The L1 term of the estimated depth compared to ground truth.
- **Time Complexity**: Geometric metrics (Acc, Comp, Chamfer) depend on the number of points $|P|$ and $|\bar{P}|$.
Naive pairwise distance computation is $O(|P| \cdot |\bar{P}|)$.
Efficient implementations use spatial indexing (e.g., KD-trees) to reduce this to approximately $O(|P| \log |\bar{P}|)$.
PSNR and Depth L1 are $O(N_I \cdot H \cdot W)$.
- **Memory Complexity**: $O(|P| + |\bar{P}|)$ to store point clouds and normals. $O(N_I \cdot H \cdot W)$ for depth maps.
- **Strengths**: Provides a holistic view of reconstruction quality by combining geometric fidelity (Acc/Comp), surface completeness (Recall/Prec), and photometric accuracy (PSNR).
The inclusion of ATE RMSE allows for direct comparison with SLAM systems.
The threshold for Completion Ratio (5 cm) is arbitrary and scene-dependent.
Normal consistency assumes aligned normals, which may not hold for all reconstruction methods.
- **When to use**: When evaluating neural scene reconstruction, INR-based SLAM, or any method producing a mesh and depth maps.

- **When not to use**: For purely static mesh quality assessment without photometric components (use [Mesh Quality Evaluation](8534-mesh-quality-evaluation.md)) or when only point cloud accuracy is needed without completeness (use [Cloud-to-Mesh Accuracy Metrics](10560-cloud-to-mesh-accuracy-metrics.md)).
